Name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
Notes: One of Europe's great small museums, ancient to modern art in a beautiful garden.

Name: MAAT - Museum of Art Architecture and Technology
Notes: Riverside contemporary art museum, striking building, great at sunset.

Name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
Notes: Portugal's tile museum inside a former convent, includes a huge pre-earthquake Lisbon tile panel.

Name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
Notes: Portugal's top collection of paintings and sculpture, with a lovely river-view garden and cafe.

Name: Torre de Belem
Notes: UNESCO-listed 16th-century tower on the Tagus.

Name: Mosteiro dos Jeronimos
Notes: Manueline masterpiece, burial site of Vasco da Gama.

Name: Padrao dos Descobrimentos
Notes: Monument to the Age of Discovery, riverside promenade.

Name: Castelo de Sao Jorge
Address: R. de Santa Cruz do Castelo, 1100-129 Lisboa
Notes: Moorish hilltop castle with the best panoramic views over the city.

Name: Cristo Rei
Notes: Christ the King statue across the river, sweeping views of Lisbon and the bridge.

Name: Palacio Nacional da Pena
Notes: Fantastical hilltop palace, the icon of Sintra.

Name: Quinta da Regaleira
Notes: Mystical estate with the famous Initiation Well and hidden tunnels.

Name: Parque Eduardo VII
Notes: Lisbon's grand central park; hosts the Feira do Livro de Lisboa (Book Fair) every year, roughly late May to mid June (2026 edition: 27 May - 14 June).

Name: Praia de Carcavelos
Notes: Wide easy-access beach on the Cascais train line, good for surfing and families.

Name: Praia do Guincho
Notes: Wild Atlantic beach near Cascais, dunes, wind and kite surfing, stunning sunsets.

Name: Praia da Adraga
Notes: Wild Sintra coast beach with cliffs and a sea cave, less crowded.

Name: Cabo da Roca
Address: Estrada do Cabo da Roca, 2705-001 Colares
Notes: Westernmost point of continental Europe, dramatic cliffs.

Name: Bairro Alto Hotel
Notes: Chic hotel right in the historic center, rooftop bar with castle views.

Name: Memmo Alfama Hotel
Notes: Boutique hotel tucked into Alfama with an unbeatable rooftop terrace.

Name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
Notes: The highest and best viewpoint in Lisbon, best at sunset.

Name: Cervejaria Ramiro
Notes: Legendary seafood spot, book ahead.

Name: LX Factory
Notes: Old factory turned creative hub with shops, murals and cafes under the 25 de Abril bridge.

Name: Time Out Market
Address: Mercado da Ribeira, Av. 24 de Julho, 1200-479 Lisboa
Notes: Food hall gathering some of the city's best kitchens under one roof.

Name: Pasteis de Belem
Notes: The original pastel de nata, since 1837.

Name: Santo António & Festas de Lisboa
Address: Avenida da Liberdade (Marchas Populares parade), Lisboa
Notes: All June, peak night 12-13 June. Lisbon's patron saint festival - arraiais (street parties) with grilled sardines across Alfama, Mouraria, Graça and Bairro Alto, plus the Marchas Populares costume parade down Avenida da Liberdade.

Name: Carnaval de Torres Vedras
Notes: February (movable, follows Carnival). Billed as the most authentically Portuguese Carnival - free entry, satirical floats and matrafonas.

Name: Feira do Livro de Lisboa (Book Fair)
Notes: Late May - mid June. Free entry, hundreds of publisher pavilions, author signings, open-air cinema.

Name: Rock in Rio Lisboa
Address: Parque do Tejo, Parque das Nações, Lisboa
Notes: Biennial (even years), late June. Multi-day City of Rock with several stages.

Name: NOS Alive
Notes: Early-to-mid July. Lisbon's flagship indie/rock/alternative festival on the riverfront.

Name: Peixe em Lisboa (food festival)
Address: Pátio da Galé, Praça do Comércio, Lisboa
Notes: April. Gastronomy festival celebrating fish and seafood with pop-up restaurants from top chefs.

Name: Rossio Christmas Market
Notes: Mid-November - late December. Wooden chalets, mulled wine, roasted chestnuts, electric Christmas train.

Name: Wonderland Lisboa
Notes: Late November - early January. Lisbon's big Christmas market: Ferris wheel, ice rink, 100+ stalls, free entry.

Name: New Year's Eve Fireworks
Notes: 31 December, midnight. Free fireworks over the Tagus plus concerts - Lisbon's biggest countdown.

Name: Cascais Old Town & Marina
Notes: Former fishing village turned elegant resort town - cobbled streets, yacht marina, 33 to 40 minute train from Cais do Sodre.

Name: Boca do Inferno
Address: Av. Rei Humberto II de Italia, Cascais
Notes: Hell's Mouth - dramatic cliffs and rock arch where the Atlantic crashes through. Free, short walk from Cascais center.

Name: Casa das Historias Paula Rego
Notes: Striking pyramid-towered museum dedicated to painter Paula Rego.

Name: National Palace of Sintra
Notes: Palace in Sintra's old town with two giant conical chimneys, a medieval royal residence.

Name: Sintra Historic Center
Notes: Fairy-tale UNESCO hill town, base for Pena Palace and Quinta da Regaleira.

Name: Costa da Caparica
Address: Costa da Caparica, across the Tagus
Notes: Lisbon's own beach, on the other side of the river: a very long stretch of Atlantic sand that guides measure at anywhere from 15 to 30 km. You do not need a car. Take the ferry from Cais do Sodré to Cacilhas and then a bus, or a direct bus over the bridge; allow about 45 to 60 minutes either way. In summer (June to September) a little tourist train, the Transpraia, runs along the southern beaches.

Name: Obidos
Notes: Walled medieval hilltop town. Hosts the International Chocolate Festival every March.

Name: Luvaria Ulisses
Notes: Tiny glove shop since 1925, last bespoke leather glove maker in Portugal. Featured in Michael Portillo's Lisbon episode.

Name: Mercado de Campo de Ourique
Address: R. Coelho da Rocha 47, Campo de Ourique
Notes: Local food hall, less touristy than Time Out Market. Featured in Michael Portillo's Lisbon episode.

Name: O Melhor Bolo de Chocolate do Mundo
Address: R. Ten. Ferreira Durao 62A, Campo de Ourique
Notes: The World's Best Chocolate Cake, tiny shop near the market. Featured in Michael Portillo's Lisbon episode.

Name: Fabrica Sant'Anna
Notes: Lisbon's oldest working tile workshop, since 1741. Featured in Michael Portillo's Lisbon episode.

Name: Bonjardim (Rei dos Frangos)
Notes: Lisbon's most famous piri-piri chicken since the 1950s. Featured in Michael Portillo's Lisbon episode.

Name: Hotel Palacio Estoril
Notes: Grand hotel where Ian Fleming stayed in 1941, inspiration for James Bond/Casino Royale. Featured in Michael Portillo's Lisbon episode.

Name: Rua dos Cegos, 20-22
Notes: 16th-century house, already ~200 years old by 1755. Projecting upper floor (andar de ressalto), devotional tile panel on facade (early-20th-century copy of the 17th-century original).

Name: Casa das Varandas - Rua dos Bacalhoeiros 8
Address: Rua dos Bacalhoeiros 8, near Casa dos Bicos
Notes: Parts predate 1755; damaged in the earthquake, rebuilt, damaged again by an 1781 fire, altered further in the 19th century.

Name: Beco de Sao Miguel
Address: Beside the Church of Sao Miguel, Alfama
Notes: Five-storey house with a dramatic overhanging upper floor - original wooden supports still visible underneath.

Name: Rua da Atalaia
Notes: Narrow, unusually tall 17th-century house, six storeys under a pointed pitched roof.

Name: Largo do Chafariz de Dentro, 32-33
Notes: Four-storey house on an ordinary Alfama square, probably 17th-century, with projecting upper floors.

Name: Praia da Rainha
Address: South of Costa da Caparica town
Notes: Further south than the town beaches and wilder, popular for swimming and surfing. In summer the Transpraia train stops along this stretch; otherwise go by car or taxi. Car helps.

Name: Fonte da Telha
Address: Far south end of the Caparica coast
Notes: The quiet end of the strip: an old fishing-village feel, beach bars serving grilled fish, fishermen working the sand and a good sunset. A bus runs here from Cacilhas, so a car is not required, but one makes the day easier. Car helps.

Name: Praia do Portinho da Arrábida
Address: Arrábida Natural Park, about 50 minutes by car
Notes: A sheltered cove with clear, calm water below the green cliffs of Arrábida. Summer rules matter: from roughly early June to mid-September (the dates shift each year), private cars are kept off the access road during the day. Park at Creiro and take the shuttle, or take the train to Setúbal and a shuttle bus from there. Outside summer there are no restrictions, and September is a good month to go. Car helps.

Name: Cabo Espichel
Address: End of the Setúbal peninsula, near Sesimbra
Notes: A windswept cape with steep cliffs, the Nossa Senhora do Cabo sanctuary, a lighthouse and fossil dinosaur footprints nearby. Sunset is the favorite time to go. Few visitors make it out here. Car helps.

Name: Parque Florestal de Monsanto
Notes: Lisbon's green lung: a big forest park with viewpoints, walking and cycling trails, picnic areas and playgrounds. Locals come here to run, bike and escape the city. It is large, so a bike, e-scooter or car lets you see much more of it. Car helps.

Name: Águas Livres Aqueduct
Notes: An 18th-century aqueduct that came through the 1755 earthquake almost undamaged. You can walk along the top, about a kilometre over 35 arches, with views across the Alcântara valley. A good head for heights helps. It is closed on Mondays, and there is a small entry fee, so check the hours first. Bus 702 from Marquês de Pombal gets you close, or take a taxi.

Name: Amoreiras Towers and 360° viewpoint
Notes: Three mirrored postmodern towers from the 1980s by the architect Tomás Taveira, with a shopping center at the base. Take the lift from the mall to the open rooftop on Tower 1, about 170 m up, for a 360-degree view of the river, the bridges and the castle. It is a good place for sunset, and there is a small entry fee.

Name: Avenida de Roma
Notes: An everyday Lisbon avenue about 2 km long, lined mostly with buildings from the Estado Novo era, old pastry shops and cafés, bookshops and independent stores. There are no sights, just a good look at how locals shop and have coffee. Roma metro station (green line) is on the avenue.

Name: Tram 28
Address: Pin shows the Martim Moniz terminus
Notes: A vintage yellow tram that climbs through Graça, Alfama, Baixa, Chiado and Estrela and ends in Campo de Ourique, about 45 to 55 minutes end to end. It is ordinary public transport, so it is packed, and a pickpocket target, from about 10:00 to 18:00. Ride early or after 18:00, and to get a seat, board at the Campo de Ourique end instead of Martim Moniz. Tram 12 covers the Alfama stretch in about 25 minutes if you are short on time.

Name: Santa Justa Lift (Elevador de Santa Justa)
Notes: A neo-Gothic iron lift from 1902, about 45 m tall, that links the Baixa with the Carmo square above. It was designed by Raoul Mesnier du Ponsard, who studied under Gustave Eiffel. The queue for the ride is often long, but the terrace at the top, next to the ruins of the Carmo Convent that the 1755 earthquake left roofless, has the same view.

Name: Oceanário de Lisboa
Address: Esplanada Dom Carlos I, Parque das Nações
Notes: A large oceanarium built for Expo 98 and designed by Peter Chermayeff, with one huge central tank that you circle twice on your way through. It works for kids and adults alike. Google lists it as open 10:00 to 19:00, so check before you go.

Name: Parque das Nações
Notes: The modern riverside district built on former industrial land for the 1998 world fair. Walk the waterfront promenade and gardens, ride the cable car (about 12 minutes along the river), look at Calatrava's Oriente station and Siza's Portugal Pavilion, and end at the Vasco da Gama Bridge. The Oceanário is here too, and the red metro line goes straight to Oriente.

Name: Restelo Hermitage (Ermida de São Jerónimo)
Notes: A small Manueline chapel from the early 16th century, and a National Monument, on the hill above Belém. It is much quieter than the monuments by the river. The grounds are open, though trees block part of the view, and the inside is usually closed except for services.
